text:
ashley: heads up — major customer (FinAppX) reporting large latency increases and intermittent 401s since ~07:12 UTC. They say requests are being routed to na-west even though their region is eu-west-1.
juan: put a pin on this. are we seeing automatic spillover triggered for eu-west?
ops-bot: alert: regional_pool_eu-west exhaustion at 07:11:43, auto-spillover engaged -> routing_policy:soft_fallback -> target_region: na-west
katie: confirmation: metrics show eu-west queue depth jumping, request latency from eu cluster to na-west ~250-400ms extra, and some auth tokens invalidating when proxied cross-region (explains 401s)
ashley: customer provided sample trace and curl repro. they hit our hosted API, many requests succeed but ~15% get routed out -> then they see 401 and retry client-side which doubles token usage and caused a billing spike for them.
emma.csm: they're pretty upset — said their usage doubled in billing overnight. can we confirm duplicate counting for retries or double-charges?
billing-bot: billing note: retries that generate new API calls count normally; duplicate 401->retry loops will increase invoiceable units. no auto-credit yet.
sri: quick hypothesis: sticky-routing depends on token-scoped session cookies. Spillover flow doesn't carry session affinity header correctly, so auth backend rejects some cross-region proxied tokens.
juan: can we reproduce internally? ashley can you drop the customer's repro curl here? also need the exact time window.
ashley: pasted below (redacted keys):

```
curl -v -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \ 
  -H 'Region: eu-west-1' \ 
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

ashley: they say executing this repeatedly during 07:10-07:20 toggles between 200 and 401 after the pool crosses the spill threshold.
katie: repro steps I used:
1) artificially reduce eu-west pool capacity on staging
2) flood with 1000 small requests/sec from eu client
3) observe queue depth, then allow spillover -> routing_policy soft_fallback
4) ~10% proxied requests return 401 when hitting auth service in na-west

katie: logs show auth proxy stripping internal header x-session-affinity when forwarding to fallback region. that's the bug.
sri: root cause likely: spillover proxy path uses a different forwarder component which wasn't updated to include x-session-affinity, so session-bound tokens are considered invalid by regional auth service (it needs the header to validate cached session state).
juan: mitigation options?
katie: short-term mitigations:
- flip soft_fallback to prefer capacity-burst instead of cross-region proxy for eu-west tenants (preference flag) — low risk config toggle
- add a temporary routing rule to pin FinAppX to eu-west while we patch forwarder
- add retry-debounce on client to avoid immediate retry on 401 (CSM communicate)

sri: medium-term: parity fix to forwarder to preserve x-session-affinity and any auth-affecting headers, plus integration tests for spillover path.
juan: does this affect billing? if retries doubled calls, we should offer a credit.
emma.csm: customer wants a credit. propose to refund incremental usage from 07:10-07:25 and offer a default account pin while we patch.
billing-bot: create ticket BILL-4829 for manual refund review. recommended refund estimate: 42k tokens (pending audit).
ashley: immediate action: applied pin to customer -> pinned to eu-west until 08:30. asked them to confirm. left a note in support ticket.
juan: can someone drop exact commands/config we used to pin? need reproducible steps for runbook.
katie: runbook snippet:

```
# pin tenant to region cli
redwoodctl tenants pin --tenant finappx --region eu-west-1 --until 2025-11-05T08:30:00Z
# verify routing table
redwoodctl routes show --tenant finappx
```

katie: also throttled background autoscaler for eu-west to force faster allocation of new workers while avoiding oscillation.
sri: I've pushed a patch to forwarder branch preserving x-session-affinity and added test that simulates auth validation post-spillover. CI green, scheduling canary to prod tonight at 23:00 UTC.
juan: schedule the canary and coordinate SRE on-call for rollback window.
ops-bot: deploy plan created: forwarder-v1.4-canary -> 23:00 UTC -> 30m -> monitor auth_401_rate, region_latency, billing_spike metric
emma.csm: customer confirmed reduced errors after pin, appreciates quick response. keeping them updated about refund.
ashley: follow-ups: (1) ensure billing audit BILL-4829 runs (2) postmortem draft after deploy (assign to katie + sri) (3) update spillover runbook to include header parity checks and pin procedure
juan: thanks team. add any logs/screenshots to the support ticket thread. closing slack thread once postmortem outline is in.
